items.text: Required receptacle is in the 6–20 ft band from the inside wall and no more than 6 ft 6 in. above the serving surface; distances checked by cord path, not through barriers.
Every 125V 15/20A receptacle within 20 ft of the inside wall is GFCI protected.
All pool motors 150V or less to ground, 60A or less (1- or 3-phase) have GFCI protection — hardwired included.
Insulated copper EGC on motor circuits, sized per 250.122 and never smaller than 12 AWG.
Bonding conductor is solid copper 8 AWG minimum with listed pressure connections; grid is continuous.
All (B)(1)–(B)(7) parts bonded: shell/steel, perimeter, metallic components, light shells, fittings over 4 in., equipment, fixed metal within 5 ft.
Perimeter ring 18–24 in. from inside walls, 4–6 in. below subgrade, minimum four uniformly spaced attachments; bonded surface extends 3 ft.
Pool water bonded — bonded part in contact, or listed water-bond surface of at least 9 sq in.
Deck/junction boxes listed as pool boxes, 4 ft minimum from inside wall, greater of 4 in. above deck or 8 in. above max water level.
Underwater luminaires listed for the niche type; wall units with lens top at least 18 in. below normal water level unless listed for less.
Overhead clearances verified from maximum water level: 22.5 ft in any direction; 14.5 ft to platforms/towers.
No underground wiring under the pool or within 5 ft except raceways serving permitted pool equipment.
New lights/fans over the pool or within 5 ft are at least 12 ft above max water; 5–10 ft band and existing fixtures meet the GFCI rules.
Photograph the bonding grid and ring before deck pour or backfill — after cover, none of it can be shown.
String voltage calculated with cold-corrected Voc (manufacturer coefficient, lowest expected ambient) and under equipment ratings; dwellings at or under 600V.
Conductor sizing shows both 690.8(B) checks (125% before factors / 100% after) — worksheet in the job folder.
String overcurrent protection applied per the 690.9 conditions, not by habit.
DC arc-fault protection present where DC circuits run at 80V or more (listed PV AFCI or equivalent).
Rapid shutdown path identified (PVHCS / 80V in 30 s inside boundary; 30V in 30 s outside the 1 ft boundary) and function-tested at final.
Initiation device readily accessible, indicates on/off; on dwellings it is outside the building.
PV disconnect readily accessible, permanently marked as the PV system disconnect.
Equipment disconnect opens all ungrounded conductors from all sources (array, grid, storage).

System rapid-shutdown label on or within 3 ft of the service disconnect, with the 690.56(C) diagram; reflective RAPID SHUTDOWN SWITCH FOR SOLAR PV SYSTEM label on or within 3 ft of the initiation device, capitals at least 3/8 in., white on red; source directory/plaque in place.
EV charging load treated as continuous: branch circuit and feeder sized at 125% of the charging load (625.41/625.42).
Receptacle outlets installed for EV charging have GFCI protection for personnel (625.54).
Where a disconnecting means is required or provided for the EVSE, it is readily accessible and within sight of the equipment (625.42/625.43 family — confirm the job's configuration).
Charge coupler is the listed type, interlocked so the vehicle connector cannot be uncoupled under load where the system requires it (625.18/625.19 family).
Spa/hot tub receptacles and the unit itself have GFCI protection as 680.44 requires — no exceptions for a listed package unit's own protection requirements.
Emergency shutoff for a spa in other than a one-family dwelling: clearly marked, readily accessible, within sight and at least 5 ft from the water (680.41).
Equipotential bonding grid installed per 680.26 for a permanently installed spa — a storable spa is the only kind outside the grid rules.
Disconnecting means for the spa equipment provided per 680.12 — readily accessible for service.
